citation.authors: Bernardi LA, Ghant MS, Andrade C, Recht H et al

cited_by.title: Heavy periods by life stage and cause

record.population: 44 premenopausal African American women, mean age 37.9, US
record.design: Cross-sectional pilot study with surveys and blood tests
record.finding: Iron deficiency was present in 68.2% and anaemia in 18.2%. Almost half said their periods were heavy or very heavy; of those, 35.0% were anaemic. Women reporting heavy periods had lower haemoglobin and ferritin than those reporting normal or light periods.
record.note: Pilot of 44 women: too small to say how common this is.

record.population: 44 premenopausal African American women, a pilot
record.finding: Iron deficiency was present in 68.2% and anaemia in 18.2%. Women who reported heavy or very heavy periods had lower haemoglobin, haematocrit and ferritin and more anaemia symptoms. Of those reporting heavy periods, 35% were anaemic. The authors recommend evaluation for iron deficiency and anaemia whenever African American women report heavy bleeding.
